messages:
liam: heads-up — saw steady memory climb on the long-context benchmark with continuous batching on. heap profile shows a lot of small KV fragments not being freed; looks like something is pinning slots during batch merge.

liam: quick pprof snippet (heap top):
```
(pprof) top10
  45.2MB  45.2MB  runtime.mcachealloc
  30.6MB  30.6MB  runtime.mspanalloc
  12.1MB  12.1MB  runtime.heapBitsForObject
  8.9MB   8.9MB   redwood/kv.(*Fragment).alloc
  6.4MB   6.4MB   redwood/serving.(*BatchMerge).holdSlots
```

maya: can you share flamegraph and the bench command you used?

liam: flamegraph: https://s3.redwood-inference/internal/flames/longctx-170812.png
bench command: `bench_longctx --ctx=65536 --qps=200 --duration=10m --cont-batch=1 --kv-pager=async`

sam: my read: when two in-flight batches merge, the merge path holds references to both headblocks until merge finalizes. if merge window grows (due to scheduling jitter or kernel stall) those refs pin the fragments and prevent pager reclaim -> memory accumulation. i think this is an HOL blocking pattern, not pure fragmentation.

nina: interesting — we also changed the async pager token backoff in last week's change. could be related. i ran a tiny local run: with `merge_ms=20` the memory peak drops ~28%, but tail latency jumps 5-7ms.

sam: agreed. limiting merge window is a blunt instrument. it trades latency for memory. alternative: allow early partial handoff of KV slots during merge via refcount handover (handoff proto: mark fragment as "handoff-in-progress", allow reads from source while target gets populated, decrement pin early).

maya: that sounds promising but tricky. we should add counters first: `kv_frag_pin_count`, `kv_frag_pin_time_ms`, `batch_merge_hold_ms` to quantify. can someone add those perf counters and a small ingestion to the console?

liam: I'll add basic counters and run a canary microbench. also noticed kernel selection sometimes picks smaller tile kernels for long sequences (to reduce memory per-op) which increases iteration count; that could keep CPU occupied longer and delay merge completion. worth correlating kernel-choice timeline with merge hold times.

nina: created dashboard panel: https://grafana.redwood/s/dash/kv-frag-hold showing pin_time, merge_hold, and heap. filling with staging metrics from earlier today.

oreg-deploy-bot: staging deploy 2024-04-18T12:30:00 - canary 3/5 checks passed (perf, smoke, auth). New image includes async-pager tuning + cont-batch toggle.

liam: repro steps for engineers who want to run locally:
```
# build with test flags
make dev && ./bin/serving --run-bench=longctx --ctx=65536 --qps=200 --cont-batch=1 --kv-pager=async
# collect heap and cpu profiles
curl -sS http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/heap > heap.pb
go tool pprof -http=:6061 ./bin/serving heap.pb
```

sam: next actions: 1) add counters (maya), 2) prototype early handoff (sam + liam), 3) run kernel-selection correlation test (nina), 4) short-term mitigation: set `merge_ms=25` in staging to avoid spikes while we investigate.

liam: i'll post flame + heap diffs by EOD. tagging @maya @sam for the handoff design review. :thumbsup:

maya: ack, moving to a small PR for counters now.

sam: pulling a quick prototype branch for handoff. will post perf numbers tomorrow.

nina: noted — i'll keep the dashboard annotated with each experiment.

liam: thanks all — main priority is to avoid long-run memory growth on live longctx workloads. will update thread with results once I have the EOD run.
